root_cause: Existing Recovery Supervisor refreshed same-repository PR branches with POST /merges without a native expected-head precondition. A concurrently advanced candidate head could change after lease readback; repeated main drift had no per-PR persisted attempt cap.
fix: Use GitHub native PUT /pulls/{number}/update-branch with expected_head_sha; check branch and main before metadata transition, require old-head and main ancestry after update, keep one writer/scheduled supervisor, preserve MAIN_SYNC for asynchronous reconciliation and bound attempts to two per PR.
prevention_rule: Never refresh an open PR from a stale head without GitHub native expected-head compare-and-swap, current exclusive lease metadata, overlap exclusion, immutable provenance readback and capped per-PR attempts. Do not bypass Required, CodeQL, preview, tenant or production gates.

required_production_proof: supervisor run confirms no repeated unsafe drift
evidence.admission_repair: Replace natural-language historical_replay values with a real executable test path; retain scenarios separately in expected_behaviors.

guardrails: one PR per supervisor recovery cycle
evaluation.status_reason: Code candidate only: provider CI and production readback not yet complete.
expected_behaviors: stale expected head returns non-success and does not update a second writer
accepted asynchronous update never marks green before immutable ancestry proof
no branch change within 10 minutes consumes bounded retry attempt
MAIN_SYNC reconciliation requires old-head and main-epoch ancestry
